https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.title: Lithospheric water contribution in geothermal systems of northern Sumatra: Insights from OLWC-based isotope reconstruction and Cl–B–Li geochemistry
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.plain_summary: This scientific study examines the sources of water in geothermal systems located in northern Sumatra by analyzing chemical markers like chlorine, boron, and lithium. Researchers used isotope reconstruction (a method of tracing the origin of elements) to understand how much water comes from deep rock layers versus other sources, which helps explain how these natural heat systems work.

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.title: Overall performance analysis of a stackable thermoelectric generator for medium-low temperature geothermal resources
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.plain_summary: Researchers have developed and analyzed a stackable thermoelectric generator (a device that converts heat directly into electricity) designed to work with medium-low temperature geothermal resources (heat from the Earth that is moderately warm rather than extremely hot). This study examines how well the generator performs when multiple units are stacked together, which could make geothermal energy more efficient for locations where the underground heat isn't extremely hot.

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.title: Evaluation of silica scaling potential for selected wells within Olkaria Domes geothermal field, Nakuru county, Kenya
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.plain_summary: Researchers studied how silica (a mineral found in rocks) builds up and hardens inside geothermal wells at the Olkaria Domes field in Kenya. This silica scaling is a common problem that can damage or block wells used to extract heat from hot rock underground, so understanding when and where it occurs helps engineers prevent costly equipment failures.

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.title: Geothermal gas geochemistry in a source-pathway-reservoir framework: review, applications, and limitations
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.plain_summary: This is a scientific review article examining how gases found in geothermal systems can be studied and understood using a 'source-pathway-reservoir' framework—essentially tracking where the gases come from, how they travel underground, and where they accumulate. The article discusses how this approach helps identify and develop geothermal resources, while also noting where this method has limitations in real-world applications.

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.title: A low-cost IoT-based accumulation chamber for measuring diffuse CO<sub>2</sub> fluxes: Design, user-friendly software, calibration, and field validation at Nea Kameni volcano (Santorini)
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.plain_summary: Researchers have developed an affordable Internet-of-Things device (a system that connects to the internet to collect data automatically) to measure carbon dioxide gas escaping from the ground at a volcano in Santorini, Greece. The tool includes easy-to-use software and was tested in the field to ensure it works accurately. This type of measurement is relevant to geothermal areas because CO2 emissions often indicate subsurface heat and activity.

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.title: Geochemistry and petrology of the Taos Plateau Volcanic Field in New Mexico: Mantle heterogeneity beneath the Rio Grande Rift and Jemez Lineament
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/ar.plain_summary: This scientific paper examines the chemical composition and rock types of the Taos Plateau Volcanic Field in New Mexico to understand variations in the Earth's mantle (the hot rock layer beneath the crust) in this region. The research looks at how the mantle differs beneath the Rio Grande Rift (a valley formed by continental stretching) and the Jemez Lineament (a geological feature in the area), which is relevant for understanding the geothermal potential of the region.

https://www.geothermalcanada.org/news/20.title: Diverso Energy Helps Developers Navigate a Shifting Market Through Flexible Geothermal Project Delivery
https://www.geothermalcanada.org/news/20.plain_summary: Diverso Energy, a Canadian geothermal company, is helping real estate developers adopt geothermal systems (which use heat from the ground to heat and cool buildings) by offering flexible project arrangements tailored to each developer's financial situation and business goals. Rather than forcing a one-size-fits-all approach, the company adjusts how projects are structured and financed to match what developers need, making geothermal technology easier to implement alongside other building systems.
